The central question: Can you turn requirements clarification, modeling and mapping, rerunnable loading, quality reconciliation and metadata delivery into a data layer that can be reviewed, reproduced and handed over, while meeting business definitions, data permissions, quality requirements and delivery deadlines?

Low-risk check: Use this page's entirely fictional order and customer materials to complete an exercise in defining the target grain, designing dimensions and facts, writing acceptance, quarantine and exclusion rules, and calculating and checking the three categories of row counts and original record amounts. Assess only your work preferences. The exercise involves no real customer data, keys or production connections and does not establish training competence or data authorization.

Worth trying first: You are willing to clarify definitions and grain before starting, accept spending considerable time on checking, reconciliation and reproducibility, have patience for detail and consistency, follow data permissions and change procedures, and explain field meanings and data limitations to business users.

The occupation itself, 15-1243.01, designs, models and implements enterprise data warehouses, configures programs and supports users. All 18 tasks are core tasks, including process models, source mapping, structural quality, metadata, testing and troubleshooting. Grain, dimension/fact tables, reruns, quarantine, reconciliation and lineage are editorial practice suggestions; this page does not claim O*NET prescribes all of them verbatim. entries: Inputs: Business definitions and target scope, source-table schemas and field samples, primary keys and update frequency, data permissions and service levels, downstream query requirements, and lists of historical failures and data quality issues.

Outputs: Dimension and fact table designs, rerunnable extract-transform-load implementations, quality assertions and quarantine mechanisms, reconciliation conclusions, metadata and lineage records, and user support notes.

Process: Clarify requirements → confirm data and permissions → define grain and models → write mappings and transformations → load and apply quality assertions → validate and reconcile → publish metadata → support users and review results. When definitions conflict, rows are anomalous or permissions are insufficient, pause, quarantine and escalate according to procedure.

description.text: Data Warehousing Specialists (O*NET-SOC 15-1243.01) design, model or implement enterprise data warehousing activities, program and configure database information repositories and support warehouse users. Tasks include source mapping, extract-transform-load processes, warehouse structures and metadata, quality checks, testing and troubleshooting. This page includes U.S. median wages for month 5 of 2025 of 139,500 dollars/year (67.07 dollars/hour), the 10th percentile of 86,240 dollars and 90th percentile of 204,000 dollars; approximately 66,900 people employed in 2024, 9% growth during 2024–2034, much faster than average, and approximately 4,000 annual openings from growth and replacement. These wages and employment use parent occupation Database Architects as a proxy. It also covers the mainland China occupational wage gap, definitions and grain, rerunnable loading, quality reconciliation and data permission boundaries.

subject.name: Data Warehousing Specialists
subject.summary: Data warehousing specialists turn dispersed source-system data into analytical data layers: define business definitions and grain, design dimension and fact models, implement rerunnable extraction, transformation and loading, check structures and data quality, maintain metadata and lineage, and support warehouse users. The basis is business definitions, data permissions and quality rules, rather than schedule pressure. The U.S. occupation is O*NET-SOC 15-1243.01 (Data Warehousing Specialists). Its wages and employment are published on that page using parent occupation Database Architects (15-1243.00) as a proxy. Mainland China's public wage statistics have not established an occupational scope corresponding to this detailed occupation; this page treats it as an evidence gap.
